indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: an instant is a moment, abbreviated MO in 'wait a mo'

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word for talk loses its final letter

parts.note: talk is chat

explanation.surface: A quick word about instant coffee, perhaps over a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instant' looks like a kind of coffee, but it is the moment in 'wait a mo'; 'Short' trims the talk word and 'on' places it after.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a type of coffee, originally from the Yemeni port of that name.

parts.note: a method is a way of doing something

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters of it's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A way of life that has turned someone into a churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' is the anagram signal, though it suits the religious surface perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: A Methodist belongs to the Protestant denomination founded by John Wesley.

indicators.note: conserving means keeping safe within, so the word for fellow holds the next letter

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A stingy man who saves on his energy bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conserving' puts E inside CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap can describe a stingy, ungenerous person, the same as mean.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters of the singer's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra annoyed a craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the seven letters of SINATRA.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker, a synonym for a craftsman.

indicators.note: misplaced letters have been put in the wrong positions, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammar pedant's warning about German spelling: the umlaut and the word 'mit' are in the wrong place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' rearranges the nine letters of UMLAUT and MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a final demand backed by a threat, i.e. a warning.

clue.text: Disorderly time in college, extremely dingy

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter for time goes into the word for college

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme, i.e. first and last, letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A student's messy time at college in a very dingy room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts T inside UNI (UNTI); 'extremely' adds D and Y from 'dingy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy means messy or not in order, a synonym of disorderly.

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A gardener's riddle: where might you have been told the hoes are kept?
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges TOLDHOES; the whole clue is also the definition, since hoes are kept in such a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden hut for tools is where hoes are stored, so the whole clue describes it.

parts.note: ma is mother, with the possessive s
a pet is a fit of sulking, a tiff or petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Mum's pet is a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' here is a sulk or huff, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a large, powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Ambassador's enthralled by sign in book

indicators.note: enthralled by means captured and held inside, so the letters go into the sign

parts.note: Taurus is a sign of the zodiac
HE (His Excellency) is the title for an ambassador, plus the possessive s

explanation.surface: An ambassador captivated by a symbol found in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE; 'enthralled by' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book of synonyms.

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin

explanation.surface: Bad weather ruins the church parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is an organised procession, a synonym of parade.

clue.text: In front of couple, score a line on rugby pitch

indicators.note: the word for score is placed in front of the word for couple

parts.note: a score is twenty
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A rugby match report: in front of the couple, someone scores a try line.
explanation.walkthrough: The twenty-two is the line 22 metres from each try line on a rugby pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The rugby field is marked with a line at twenty-two metres from each goal line, known by that number.

clue.text: Use obscene language in southern sport

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them

explanation.surface: Players in a southern sport cursing on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' is a verb here: to sport a hat is to wear it.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse or utter profanities is the plain meaning.

parts.note: to pose a question is to suggest it, so suggested gives posed

explanation.surface: Someone stands against the operation that was suggested.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something means being against it: a direct synonym.

clue.text: After opening of shop, steal, pocketing a vegetable

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay comes after that opening letter
the opening of a word is its first letter
pocketing means holding inside, so the word for steal takes in the next piece

parts.note: to pinch is to steal

explanation.surface: A shoplifter slips a vegetable into a pocket just as the shop opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketing' puts A inside PINCH to give PINACH, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable.

parts.note: a fan is something that cools

explanation.surface: A midwife delivers a baby at a cooler temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivers' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child, a synonym for a baby.

clue.text: Female secure around spacious place of enchantment

indicators.note: around here means next to, so the word for secure sits alongside the word for spacious

parts.note: an airy room is open and spacious
to land a deal or a fish is to secure it

explanation.surface: A woman secures a roomy, magical place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' cannot mean enclosing here; it only signals the pieces sit next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairyland is the magical realm of fairies, a place of enchantment.

parts.note: a set is a group
the Forth is a river in Scotland flowing into the Firth of Forth at Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A walking party sets off from beside a river in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To set forth is to depart on a journey, meaning to leave.

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: A bullied husband who gets only a quick kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Henpecked describes someone, usually a husband, nagged and dominated by a partner, the same as browbeaten.

clue.text: Novitiate, one they ordered to keep quiet

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the rearranged letters take in the next piece
ordered means arranged anew, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A novice in a religious order who has been told to keep silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges the two words into NEOHYTE; 'to keep' then holds the quiet letter, P being piano in music.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a newcomer or beginner, especially a new convert, like a novitiate.

clue.text: Brief word about weird sister, keen birdwatcher

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes around the next piece
brief means shortened, so the word for word loses its last letter

parts.note: a term is a word
the Weird Sisters are the three witches in Macbeth

explanation.surface: A short remark about one of Macbeth's witches, made by an eager birdwatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weird Sisters are Macbeth's three witches; 'Brief' trims the last letter, leaving TER, and 'about' wraps it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a twitcher is an enthusiast who travels to spot rare birds.

parts.note: a collie is a breed of sheepdog

explanation.surface: A dog that is just right for a mining family.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner.

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter for son goes into the word for club

parts.note: a club or society can be called a union

explanation.surface: A son plays in a club concert.
explanation.walkthrough: UNION is opened as UNI|ON to admit S.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting together, the same sense as in unison.

clue.text: Agree to collect travel document in Serbian port

indicators.note: to collect means to gather in, so the word for agree takes the document inside

parts.note: to nod is to show agreement
a visa is a document permitting travel to a country

explanation.surface: Someone nods to collecting a visa for a trip to Serbia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to collect' signals that the travel document goes inside the word for agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Novi Sad is a city in Serbia on the Danube, with a river port.

clue.text: Artist's after nuts for a curry

indicators.note: the artist piece comes after the word for nuts

parts.note: nuts means mad, crazy
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist, plus the possessive s

explanation.surface: An artist who is crazy about curry.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is a Royal Academician; 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A madras is a fairly hot style of Indian curry, named after the city now called Chennai.

clue.text: Record of wages, say, stupidly left in spot

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go into the word for spot

parts.note: a pip is a spot, as on dice or cards

indicators.note: acting stupidly suggests things put in a muddled order, so the letters of say are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly left their pay record lying in a certain spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like an example marker but is fodder; 'stupidly' gives AYS, and 'in' splits the spot word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A payslip is the note an employee gets showing what they earned.

definitions.meaning: coming earlier in time or order
the monk ranking just below an abbot in an abbey

explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier; it is also the title of the second-in-command of an abbey.
To advance is to move forward, and an advance is also money lent or paid beforehand.

clue.text: Sound of hooter I put in

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so the letter goes inside the word for hooter

parts.note: hooter is British slang for a nose

explanation.surface: The honk from a hooter that I've installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' is a car horn on the surface but slang for a nose; 'put in' puts I inside NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise is any sound, especially a loud one.

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: A piece of china turned up in a river in Hiroshima.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' points to the letters across 'HiroshIMA RIver'.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is a style of Japanese porcelain exported from the port of Imari.

indicators.note: facing means set in front of, so the word for court comes first

parts.note: a courtyard or yard is an enclosed court
stick is informal British for harsh criticism, as in 'giving someone stick'

explanation.surface: A ruling in court that faces criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' as criticism is British slang; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a measuring rod, hence a standard or rule to judge by.

clue.text: With no one up slide, errs foolishly

indicators.note: doing something foolishly suggests disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone goes down a slide with nobody on top and makes foolish mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges SLIDE and ERRS.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with no jockey up, i.e. no one riding it, is described this way.

parts.note: a gauge that showed a value read it, as in 'the meter read zero'

explanation.surface: A daughter shows that she is afraid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension: a synonym.
